title: S014 — Fold-state delta / long-horizon timeline traversal
description: Test whether S012's validated FoldStateDelta retention can make long-horizon timeline traversal cheaper while preserving EXACT derive() semantics for every prefix (not just the terminal state).
result_summary: Promising but experimental. Retained traversal (keep H[j] iff foldStateDeltas components non-empty) is exactly prefix-correct: 0 mismatches on all 1001 prefixes at H=1000, all 3001 at H=3000, 302 sampled at H=10000, and the S009/S010 witnesses. Branch isolation and determinism pass; derive() remains the sole semantic authority. Performance is workload-dependent: sparse retention (0.6-0.7%) gives 6.88x/6.69x speedup; medium/dense (~47% retention) gives 0.87x-1.10x (no benefit); H=10000 gives 1.12x/1.46x. The bottleneck is the per-prefix propagation fixpoint (O(model)), which retention does not touch. H=50k/100k not run (O(H^2) traversal without incremental propagation).
bottleneck: per-prefix propagation fixpoint (propagateJudgments), O(model), unchanged by retention
next_experiment: incremental propagation - recompute only the affected subgraph of the fixpoint per step; that is what would let retention's chain reduction become an end-to-end traversal speedup for dense timelines.
limitations: H=50k/100k not measured (O(H^2) traversal without incremental propagation).
Medium and dense workloads coincide (~47% retention) in this generator.
Harness slice/filter bookkeeping is included in retained timings and slightly penalises it.
